# Kō 1.3.0 release verification

Stable GitHub release dated 22 October 2026, prepared for `master` and tag `v1.3.0`. Both manifest version fields are `1.3.0`. The manual and store-layout ZIPs include the companion, gallery, English JMdict and Japanese Wiktionary dictionaries. Chrome Web Store submission and publication are separate from this release.

## Behavior

Kōくん starts off and has an independent popup switch. Pause on this site hides him. One transparent companion appears in the top-level HTTP/HTTPS webpage viewport, with per-site drop positions, keyboard repositioning, three sizes, and system/still motion preferences. Hidden tabs suspend playback; printing and fullscreen hide him.

The ambient scheduler starts awake, with 12–24 second pauses between actions, rounded up to a complete 2.4-second idle cycle. Standing and seated idle use the authored blink and breathing loops, retaining all four limbs and three tails. Sleep alone holds its first loop frame and checks time four times per second. Sleep cannot be selected until three active-tab minutes have elapsed and at least three walking trips have been scheduled; each subsequent sleep has the same requirements. Eligible rests have a 12% sleep chance and last 60–120 seconds when selected. The first three ordinary activities are walks; subsequent ordinary choices have a 65% walking chance and 7% floating chance. Ambient travel is limited to 80 px walking or 48 px floating at the default size. Eight special routines rotate with a 5–10 minute active-tab cooldown, performed at the next activity opportunity; ambient specials use one loop. Activity loops remain capped at two. Playback preserves timing across cached clip boundaries and gently blends repeated closing seams, retaining authored entry and exit poses.

Showing a word immediately selects the open-scroll reading loop at frame zero, followed by its normal exit after one 2.4-second cycle. Reading takes priority over all 24 routines, including idle, sleep, travel, and costumes, without waiting for their entries, loops or exits. The visible horizontal location, ground height, and saved drop area are preserved. An airborne companion settles to his existing ground over 1.2 seconds while the scroll is already animating. The read-loop strip is preloaded and retained within the six-strip cache so an unrelated routine cannot evict the first reading frame. Dismissing the bubble lets reading finish its normal exit; further words during the reading loop update the bubble without freezing or restarting it. A reading arriving during the exit immediately reopens the scroll. The existing reviewed artwork supplies these behaviors, with no new generated poses. Reduced motion keeps the still character and word bubble.

Clicking Kōくん wakes him with a greeting and enables more activity for 60 seconds of elapsed time, including time spent in a background tab. Repeated clicks refresh the deadline instead of stacking extra minutes. The click boost inserts 8–16 second animated idle pauses, rounded up to a full cycle, between actions and allows slightly longer local journeys (96 px walking, 72 px floating at the default size). Enter and Space activate the same behavior. Dragging, cancelled pointer gestures and arrow-key repositioning do not wake him; a drop cancels movement and establishes a new animated idle. Expiration returns the next scheduled choice to an ambient idle, allowing a routine underway to complete its normal exit. Reduced-motion preferences take precedence over wake activation.

Movement is sampled from the same active-time clock as sprite playback. Walking and trotting accelerate and decelerate through their start and stop clips, finish exactly at their destinations, and retain the artwork's maximum travel speeds. Airborne routines rise 36 px at the default 128 px size, hover with a gentle 2 px bob, and finish with the authored landing clip during ordinary routines; immediate reading uses the settling motion described above. Floating travel stays horizontal; landing restores the original ground height. Ninja sneaking moves up to 24 px per loop, fan dancing steps up to 6 px and returns, and sword practice and the straw-hat punch shift forward up to 4 px and return. Other routines retain their planted positions and authored gestures. Distances scale with character size and shorten at viewport or reading-panel boundaries.

Flight height and temporary action offsets are separate from the remembered ground position. Dragging or keyboard placement during flight rebases the visible location as the new ground position, cancels movement, and preserves the remaining pose exits without a second descent. Bubble positioning follows the displayed character. Hidden tabs, fullscreen and printing suspend movement; decoding waits do not accumulate catch-up movement. Reduced motion or missing assets clear movement offsets and show the still character. The PS1 artwork replacement retains the existing settings schema and storage formats.

Hover waits 600 ms and closes immediately when the pointer leaves the resolved source word, including inline text, Docs geometry, and reading-view words. Moving within that word keeps the bubble open without restarting lookup. Highlight mode accepts one Japanese word. Readings and saved corrections stay local. Definitions are separately off by default. English now uses bundled JMdict first, with English Wiktionary fallback; Japanese now uses a bundled Japanese Wiktionary snapshot first, with the same online fallback rule. The bubble retains readings during network failure, rejects stale replies, and renders extracted remote text without active markup. Mascot analysis has a separate request/cancellation purpose from page readings and Playgrounds.

Web lookup supports inline text, native ruby, and accessible open shadows. Google Docs uses exposed text geometry and known fonts, with reading-view word hooks as the fallback. Native Docs text selection is supported only where the browser exposes a real selection. Embedded-frame lookup, closed third-party shadows, arbitrary canvas/image text, browser-protected pages, and browser PDF viewers are excluded. Browser toolbar and tab-strip areas are outside the mascot viewport.

## Timing rationale

The timing choices were informed by an online review on 19 October 2026. [Nielsen Norman Group](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/animation-usability/) explains how peripheral movement draws attention away from reading. [Microsoft's desktop animation guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/uxguide/vis-animations) recommends brief, subtle animation, reserving stronger effects for infrequent events; its 1–3 second recommendation concerns attention-getting effects, not a tested vPet cadence. [W3C's Pause, Stop, Hide guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pause-stop-hide.html) emphasizes control over automatically moving content presented alongside reading material. Kō retains its off switch and still-character option.

The revised 12–24 second ambient idle pauses, delayed sleep, increased walking, 5–10 minute special cooldown and 8–16 second click-boost pauses follow the requested behavior. These are product defaults, not experimentally validated vPet intervals. Existing authored routines can take longer than three seconds to complete their entry, action and exit, so the implementation limits their frequency and loop counts and preserves safe pose transitions instead of cutting clips abruptly.

## About animation gallery

Click the version number on About Kō five times, or activate the focused version button with Enter or Space, to open `animations.html` in the same tab. Browser Back returns to About. Thirty small labeled tiles cover all 24 routines and six transitions, automatically playing all 56 clips with no controls. The gallery uses only bundled assets, loads tiles as they enter the viewport, suspends playback in hidden tabs and shows still previews for system reduced motion. Both development ZIP layouts include its HTML and JavaScript.

## Verification

- Consolidated WIP verification on 19 October 2026: **225 tests passed**, with no failures or skips, using `npx playwright test --reporter=line`. This includes the native toolbar popup, the final PS1 companion and its current motion/reading behavior, and existing furigana, Docs, dictionaries, preferences, forms, mimetics and update announcements. Earlier stage-specific results below remain historical evidence.
- TypeScript typecheck and extension build pass.
- Idle, reading-reaction and movement regression run: **37 passed** using `npx playwright test tests/mascot-motion.spec.ts tests/mascot-playback.spec.ts tests/mascot.spec.ts tests/mascot-dictionary.spec.ts`. This includes all 24 routines at 96, 128 and 160 px, continuous clip boundaries, exact landing and travel endpoints, movement bounds, drag/keyboard rebasing, animated standing/seated rests, still sleeping frames, low-frequency sleeping timers, immediate open-scroll reactions from all 24 routines and one-cycle exits, click/keyboard wake activation, minute expiry, reduced motion, and Google Docs lookup. The Docs hover fixture now waits for the companion to be visible before moving its pointer, avoiding a storage-update readiness race.
- Deterministic ambient scheduling checks require over 60% of ordinary activities to be walks, and prohibit sleep before three active minutes and three walks. Adversarial sleep-favoring randomness verifies the minimum delay. These are regression checks of the chosen defaults, not a user study. Visual contact sheets for all three sizes are saved as `qa/release-1.3/movement-routines-{96,128,160}.png` and were reviewed for placement and clipping.
- Pre-movement integration regression run: **209 passed** using `npx playwright test --grep-invert 'native toolbar popup'`. The one excluded native-window check is documented below; it was attempted separately and blocked by window focus.
- Browser frame comparisons cover all 672 production frames in both directions: 1,344 exact canvas comparisons. The decoded-strip cache remains bounded to six entries.
- The PS1 replacement passes the same 37 mascot checks. Asset verification also decodes all 27 animated previews, checks 76 canonical endpoints and 26 phase joins, verifies all 16 reversed clips, and flags no loop-seam outliers. The offline review gallery passes 56 clip-control checks, 168 stepped-frame samples, mirrored views and four backgrounds without page errors or remote requests. Anatomy is recorded separately through direct visual review of every accepted source pose.
- All 24 routines connect from every delivered pose and return through valid exits. Tests cover special cooldowns, rotation, a two-iteration activity cap, nearby destinations, and seam smoothing that preserves the last exit pose.
- Browser checks verify immediate dismissal off a hovered word, continued reading animation with an open bubble, word-length sizing, Japanese pixel font loading, narrow-viewport wrapping, live movement and scaled speed, drag/keyboard placement, reload persistence, reduced motion, visibility/fullscreen, printing, absent strips, hover cancellation, highlights, kana, inflections, reading corrections, Docs geometry, reading-view hooks, restrictive CSP, and stale online replies.
- Preference-writer checks cover concurrent changes, malformed values, position reset, and bounded per-site storage. Request tests cover analysis-channel isolation and definition-language compatibility.
- Offline About, privacy, and release-history pages pass 12 viewport checks at 1280, 700, 390, and 320 px, without horizontal overflow, remote requests, or page errors. See `qa/release-1.3/offline-docs.json`.
- The About gallery passes five-click and keyboard activation, all 56 clips playing across 30 tiles, offline use, no controls, reduced-motion stills, and a 320 px layout without overflow or page errors. See `qa/release-1.3/animation-gallery.json` and run `node qa/release-1.3/check-gallery.cjs` to repeat the check.
- All 52 local Markdown links in the README and top-level documentation resolve.
- The native toolbar auto-sizing check **passes in the consolidated run**, including its 580 px height, collapsed footer fit and expanded scrolling. Earlier macOS focus failures described above do not apply to this final run. A separate 380 × 580 browser check also verifies settings persistence and footer access.

## Dialogue style

The dialogue uses content-sized widths, wrapped text, a muted sage/paper/ink palette, subtle checker dithering, square beveled borders, a stepped tail, and the bundled DotGothic16 Japanese pixel font. Its glyphs load from extension assets on first lookup, without a remote font service. The original font and its SIL Open Font License are in `public/art/fonts/`; upstream source: [Google Fonts DotGothic16](https://github.com/google/fonts/tree/main/ofl/dotgothic16).

## Assets and local packages

The approved PS1 design replaces all 56 sprite strips and the static fallback. The library retains all 24 routines and 672 exported RGBA timeline frames. Forty generated source sheets supply the motion; sixteen exits, stops, wake and landing clips reverse reviewed poses. All 480 source poses received direct visual review for four actual limbs and three tails. Five thinking-source poses with a fourth tail are excluded; that gesture uses seven verified head-tilt poses and a deliberate hold. The packager checks that rejected poses cannot enter the timeline. Rejected variants with duplicated forelegs, cropped props or poor recovery remain in the QA archive. Pixel checks do not establish anatomy.

Uniform export registration aligns independently generated sheets with shared connection poses. Every non-looping clip has pixel-identical canonical endpoints; phase boundaries are checked in both directions. Flight loops have export-placement drift removed because the runtime supplies continuous hovering and bobbing. No intermediate poses are synthesized by the packaging scripts. The offline [PS1 review gallery](../qa/ko-kun-animation/ps1-review.html) includes all routines, frame stepping, speed controls, mirrored views, and several backgrounds. Sources, exact prompts, provenance, anatomy notes and technical reports are under `qa/ko-kun-animation/ps1/`. The earlier artwork remains in the historical production archive.

`npm run package:release` generates the manual ZIP with a `dist/` prefix and the store ZIP with the manifest at its root. `python3 qa/release-1.3/verify-packages.py` verifies identical runtime files, stable version metadata, gallery HTML/JavaScript, accepted PS1 asset digests, 90 mimetic strips, all 56 mascot clips, both dictionary snapshots and notices, exclusions, and `SHA256SUMS`. Exact counts, sizes and checksums are recorded in `qa/release-1.3/packages.json`. ZIPs are ignored by Git and uploaded as GitHub release assets; source, compiled runtime, notices and verification reports are committed.

Reload the extension from the rebuilt `dist/` folder, then reload open tabs. Enable Kōくん in the extension popup. Existing settings and corrections remain intact.

## Local-first dictionary integration · 22 October 2026

The release includes the complete English JMdict snapshot (218,942 entries) in 256 compressed lookup shards. English local hits make no external request; Missing local meanings automatically use the selected Wiktionary edition. Reading-panel languages load independently. Canonical spelling references such as 飲む → のむ are resolved within the same edition, with bounded hops and one eight-second deadline. Unsupported layouts offer retry instead of becoming cached missing definitions. JMdict source metadata, documentation, and its separate CC BY-SA licence ship in both ZIP layouts.

See the [dictionary verification report](../qa/release-1.3/local-dictionary.md) for root causes, test runs, memory bounds, timings, and package sizes. Before source integration, the final dictionary/importer/security rerun passed all 12 tests; the offline documentation check passed 12 page/viewport combinations with no overflow, network requests, or errors. Typecheck, whitespace checks, and package-content parity passed. These dictionary checks preceded stable release preparation; they did not submit the extension to the store.

## Offline Japanese definitions · 22 October 2026

A pinned Japanese Wiktionary extract now supplies Japanese explanations locally alongside English JMdict meanings. It covers 124,195 headwords, including 11,252 spelling references resolved during import. Ambiguous, contradictory, missing and cyclic references remain online fallbacks. The importer checks that reference metadata agrees with the gloss and does not infer general reading aliases, preventing unrelated homophones from being merged. Both languages share bounded shard/result caches.

Source JSONL is pinned with full-export and filtered-snapshot checksums. The raw export has an HTTP Last-Modified date of 3 October 2026; it is separate from the newer postprocessed website data. Bundled shards include Japanese definitions, source titles, parts of speech, readings and sense labels, with examples, translations and media omitted. Japanese Wiktionary contributor and Kaikki/Wiktextract attribution and CC BY-SA notices ship in both package layouts.

See the [Japanese dictionary verification report](../qa/release-1.3/japanese-dictionary.md) and [source/refresh notes](../data/jawiktionary/README.md) for coverage, limitations, tests, package sizes and measured lookup timings.

## Stable release preparation · 22 October 2026

The compact popup announcement now includes **Try Kōくん**, which opens his settings and focuses the opt-in switch without enabling him. Dismissal is stored once for 1.3.0 on this device and survives popup/browser restarts. Existing pre-release 1.3.0 dismissals remain honored. Documentation and download links now identify the stable release.

Latest runtime changes include dictionary-backed kanji noun compounds, local Japanese definitions, Google Docs painted single-word selection lookup with ambiguous/multi-line rejection, and safe content-script skipping of direct SVG/XML documents. Earlier test runs above describe their dated stages; final release checks are recorded below.

Final validation: build and TypeScript typecheck pass. The full 245-case Playwright run completed with 244 passes and one offline-lookup failure while packaging concurrently rebuilt dictionary assets. That exact case passed on a focused rerun against the completed build. All 245 cases are therefore verified, with the initial failure retained here rather than reported as a clean full-suite pass. The two invitation tests also pass separately, including opt-in focus, restart persistence, cross-popup synchronization and failed-save retry. Native toolbar sizing passed in the full run.

Offline About, privacy and release history pass all 12 page/viewport checks with no overflow, remote requests or errors. The offline gallery passes all 56 clips across 30 tiles, keyboard/five-click entry and reduced motion. All 63 local Markdown links in the README and top-level docs resolve. Package verification confirms 728 byte-identical runtime files across both ZIP layouts, required dictionary notices, accepted art digests, exclusions and SHA-256 checksums. `git diff --check` passes. Generated media drafts and service receipts under `output/` remain local; approved promotional assets are retained under `docs/`.

## Chrome Web Store package compatibility · 22 October 2026

The first store upload was rejected because Chrome Web Store found four files named `manifest.json`: the extension root manifest and the mascot, English dictionary, and Japanese dictionary metadata. No new package draft was accepted from that attempt.

The build now ships those three internal data indexes as `index.json`. Mascot playback, the animation gallery, and the web-accessible resource declaration use the renamed animation index. Source authoring metadata keeps its original filename. Dictionary shards, animation artwork, permissions, and version 1.3.0 are unchanged. Packaging and the release verifier now reject nested extension manifests.

The corrected manual/store ZIPs have the same 728 runtime files and exactly one extension manifest. The store ZIP is 102,617,608 bytes with SHA-256 `ce7e5c459134aa9b4f99fb44f2a1f599d94f66aa9ffc9d50d34af97fc6a5d504`; the manual ZIP is 102,625,008 bytes with SHA-256 `dd673c00b38b0c6d6fec9fc56648bcf2d9d21443f737bfdd492b70ce34e5d5f8`. These local corrections do not replace the already-published GitHub release assets or tag.

Build, typecheck, package verification, and `git diff --check` pass. The full 245-case run passed 231 cases and exposed 14 playback-harness failures because that harness served source assets under the old metadata path. Updating the harness to serve built assets fixed all 14 on a focused rerun. All 245 cases are verified across those runs; the initial run was not a clean pass. The corrected gallery checks all 56 clips across 30 tiles, offline loading, reduced motion, and keyboard/five-click entry. All 12 offline documentation page/viewport checks pass.

The owner approved the updated description, project/support links, five store-sized screenshots, local-first privacy explanations, reviewer instructions, and corrected-package upload. Store submission requires a separate final confirmation. Automatic publication must remain disabled. Store draft and review status must be verified in the dashboard before reporting submission complete.

The saved description, homepage/support links, privacy explanations, reviewer instructions, and five screenshots were verified. The approved screenshot order was restored and saved after an unintended reorder. The final submission dialog is open with automatic publication unchecked (`Value: 0`); the final **Send for review** action is awaiting owner confirmation.
